title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is sketching a programme of crystalline Dieudonné theory, in the line of his 1970 Nice ICM talk, Messing's thesis and the 1974 Montréal lectures.

Characteristic p part.
- Setup. S_o has characteristic p and G_o is a Barsotti–Tate group over it. M = D*(G_o) is its Dieudonné crystal, and M_o is the restriction of M to the crystalline site of S_o relative to F_p.
- The map φ. Let φ : (S_o/F_p)_cris → S_o be the morphism of ringed topoi introduced earlier in the notes. It is a Frobenius-twisted version of the projection ε. On a PD-thickening T of S_o in characteristic p, the Frobenius of T factors through S_o, because x^p = p!·x^[p] = 0 on the PD ideal. Hence φ*(M_{S_o}) ≅ M_o^(p).
- Exactness. The previous page asserts that M_o^(p) →F→ M_o →V→ M_o^(p) →F→ M_o is exact on every thickening.
- Claim on this page. The Hodge filtration Fil^1 ⊂ M_{S_o} (the sub-bundle ω_G) satisfies φ*(Fil^1) = Ker F = Im V ⊂ M_o^(p).
- Uniqueness. φ is 'faithful' enough that this relation determines the locally direct summand Fil^1 uniquely. So Fil^1 is not extra structure: it is determined by the Dieudonné crystal with F and V.
- Admissibility. An F-V-crystal (or Dieudonné crystal) is called admissible if such a Fil^1 exists; it is then unique and is called the canonical filtration. Crystals coming from BT groups are admissible, and their canonical filtration is the Hodge filtration. This answers the worry on the previous page that 'Problem 1' (full faithfulness / essential image of D*) should be posed with filtered Dieudonné crystals.

Section 3: abelian schemes, with no privileged prime.
- One works on the nilpotent crystalline site and sets D*(A) = R^1 f_{cris*} O_{A_cris}, a contravariant functor to locally free crystals.
- Base change gives D*(A)_S = H^1_dR(A/S).
- For a nilpotent PD-thickening S' of S and any lift A'/S', one gets D*(A)_{S'} = H^1_dR(A'/S'). The next page continues with the Hodge filtration and the Grothendieck–Messing-type deformation theorem: lifts correspond to lifts of ω_A ⊂ D*(A)_{S'}.

Marginal plan items:
- (d) passage to the limit: a formula for A perfect and p-adically complete;
- (e) isogenies, tori and Tate's theorem;
- (f) duality.
errors: The faithfulness of φ ensuring uniqueness of Fil^1 is asserted without proof. Frobenius of S_o alone kills nilpotents, so uniqueness must use evaluation on PD-thickenings (e.g. a PD-envelope of S_o in a smooth scheme), not just S_o. The claim is plausible but non-trivial for non-reduced bases and is left as 'on montre'.
Minor typos: 'filtra- canonique' (filtration), 'au dessus' corrected from 'dessous', 'déterminé' agreement.

ideas.what: Hodge filtration of a Dieudonné crystal in char p is characterized by φ*(Fil^1) = Ker F = Im V on M^(p)
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration as Frobenius descent of Ker F / conjugate–Hodge relation (Oda-type relation ω^(p) = Ker F = Im V)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oda (1969) over perfect fields for H^1_dR of abelian varieties; Grothendieck ICM 1970; Berthelot–Breen–Messing (1982) in general
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux' (ICM 1970) / Montréal notes 1974

ideas.what: Notion of 'admissible' F-V-crystal / Dieudonné crystal: one whose Ker F descends uniquely along φ to a locally direct summand of M_{S_o}
ideas.modern_name: Admissible Dieudonné crystal; cf. later conditions in de Jong's and Lau's/Zink's Dieudonné theory over non-perfect bases
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programme), later de Jong 1995, Lau, Zink

ideas.what: Crystalline Dieudonné functor for abelian schemes on the nilpotent crystalline site, D*(A) = R^1 f_cris* O, with value H^1_dR on any lift
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline H^1 of abelian schemes / Grothendieck–Messing–Mazur–Messing theory
ideas.where_published: ICM Nice 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'

ideas.what: Marginal plan: Dieudonné theory over perfect p-adically complete rings via passage to the limit

missed.claim: Grothendieck asserts, without proof, that the Hodge filtration of a Dieudonné crystal over an arbitrary char-p base is uniquely recoverable from (M, F, V) via faithfulness of the crystalline Frobenius morphism φ. He defines 'admissible' crystals as those for which it exists, aiming to remove the filtration from the formulation of the classification problem.
missed.quote: on montre que φ a des propriétés de fidélité telles que la relation précédente détermine sans ambiguité le sous-Module localement facteur direct Fil^1 de M_{S_o}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Over non-reduced, non-smooth bases the question of whether the Dieudonné crystal alone (without Hodge filtration) determines and classifies BT groups is subtle (de Jong, Lau, Zink). An explicit 'admissibility' condition as a candidate essential-image criterion is a clean formulation that seems not to appear verbatim in the literature.

missed.claim: Margin plans a limit formula for p-adically complete perfect rings, a treatment of isogenies, tori and Tate's theorem, and duality, inside the crystalline programme.
missed.quote: d) Passage à la limite : formule pour anneau A parfait complet pour top. p-adique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates later Dieudonné theory over perfect/perfectoid rings (Gabber, Lau, Scholze–Weinstein), though only as a heading.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly the known Grothendieck crystalline-Dieudonné programme (ICM 1970, Messing, Mazur–Messing). The admissibility criterion via φ-faithfulness over arbitrary char-p bases is a notable unpublished detail with uncertain coverage in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'sous-module loc. facteur direct Fil^1 de M_{oS}' — the image reads M_{o S_o}, i.e. M_o evaluated at S_o.
'Ce Fil^1 est unique et M' — the inserted handwritten M appears to start a new sentence ('On dit de même...'), so read roughly 'Ce Fil^1 est unique. On dit de même...'.
'la filtra- canonique' should read 'la filtration canonique'.
In (*) the handwritten correction gives O_{A_cris} as the structure sheaf of A_cris (the typed 'Acris*' subscript denotes f_{A cris *}).
